subject: Horizon Dataworks trial — success roadmap, KPIs & owners
messages:
From: Alex Grove <alex@horizondw.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya@horizondw.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / trial discussion (Horizon)

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the quick call earlier. Priya and I reviewed notes and want to make sure we're aligned on what success looks like for a 3-week technical trial. High level asks from our side: 

- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 500ms for single-turn queries (our most common conversational path).
- Throughput: sustain 120 rps peak with average payload of ~350 tokens.
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0009 for inference (we can adjust if quantization affects quality).
- Quality: 4.2+ NPS-style score on the evaluation set of 250 prompts (we'll share samples).

We also need a simple runbook for troubleshooting and a named eng contact in case we hit perf cliffs. Can you confirm Redwood can provide a test config + estimated GPU footprint so we can sign procurement?

Attachments: horizon_poc_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Alex
Director, AI Platforms
Horizon Dataworks
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grove <alex@horizondw.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@horizondw.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intro / trial discussion (Horizon)

Alex / Priya — great to meet you both. Recap + proposed trial runway below. Please let me know any gaps.

Recap of success criteria (from call + your email):
- Latency: p95 <= 500ms for canonical single-turn queries (we'll validate with your 250 prompt set)
- Throughput: able to sustain 120 rps peak with ~350 token average payloads
- Cost: target <= $0.0009/token (we'll model 16-bit vs 8-bit quantized profiles)
- Quality: aggregate quality score >= 4.2/5 on your evaluation prompts (we'll run blind evals)

Proposed 3-week technical trial (timeline):
Week 0 (this week): exchange eval prompt set, sample workload, and enable sandbox keys. Redwood provides baseline perf matrix and cost estimate.
Week 1: smoke tests + latency tuning (prefix caching, batching params). Daily sync as needed.
Week 2: scale run and sustained throughput runs; quality evaluation on full 250 prompts.
Week 3: run long-tail/edge-case tests, finalize runbook and handoff to your ops/procurement for committed capacity.

Owners / points of contact:
- Redwood technical lead (perf & tuning): Ben Carter — ben_carter@redwood.com
- Redwood account + trial coordinator: Evelyn Hart — evelyn_hart@redwood.com
- Redwood infra escalation: David Kim — david_kim@redwood.com

Action items (we'll track in the Drive link):
1) You: drop the 250 prompt file + representative workload traces in the Drive link.
2) We: deliver a baseline perf/cost matrix and a recommended config by EOD Friday.
3) Proc: we can float a small trial PO if procurement needs a number to lock resources — happy to coordinate.

Attachments: horizon_trial_success_matrix.xlsx (initial, editable)

I'll queue Ben for an intro session tomorrow to walk through config knobs. Sound good?

Best,
Evelyn
Head of Customer Trials
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Alex Grove <alex@horizondw.com>, Priya Suresh <priya@horizondw.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / trial discussion (Horizon) — perf plan & quick win knobs

Alex / Priya — thanks, adding a few technical clarifications so expectations are explicit: 

1) Baseline config we'll test (first 48 hours): 2x A40-like instances per replica, dynamic batching enabled, prefix cache cold-start disabled for reproducibility. Expected baseline: p95 ~380-520ms depending on prompt length; cost modeled at $0.00095/token for fp16 kernels.

2) Speedups & cost levers we'll try (and owner):
- 8-bit quantization (Ben): may reduce cost ~30% but we must validate quality drop on your eval set.
- Aggressive batching (Ben + Redwood runtime): tune to hit 120 rps sustained while keeping tail latency under p95 target.
- Prefix-level KV caching (David): once warm, this will drop p95 significantly for repeated prompts.

3) Success gating rubric (automated checks we'll run nightly):
- Perf gate: 95th percentile <= 500ms for the official 250 prompts under 120 rps sustained for 30 minutes.
- Throughput gate: sustained 120 rps for 30 minutes with <5% request failures.
- Cost gate: projected per-token inference cost <= $0.0009 using the chosen config.
- Quality gate: mean rating >= 4.2 across your blind eval set (we'll use randomized ordering).

4) Runbook stub we'll hand you by Week 1 end: escalation steps, what logs to collect (latency histograms, GPU utilization, KV hit rate), and temporary mitigations (scale replicas, conservative batching).

Next steps: Evelyn to share Drive link & we (Ben + David) will schedule a 60-min technical kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT. Procurement folks: if you want a provisional PO, we can provide an estimated monthly burn for the trial config.

Cheers,
Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Suresh <priya@horizondw.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Alex Grove <alex@horizondw.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, procurement@horizondw.com
Date: 2027-05-05T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / trial discussion (Horizon) — perf plan & quick win knobs

Thanks everyone — that plan works for us. A few clarifications from our side before the kickoff: 

- We will upload the 250 prompts and a small trace dump (representative 48-hour window) to the Drive link by EOD today.
- For quality scoring we'll use a 1–5 rubric; can Redwood confirm the blind eval tooling & whether we can add a separate bias/ hallucination check?
- Procurement: provisional PO is helpful. Procurement (cc) — can you advise any required paperwork? We aim to sign a trial PO by next Wednesday to reserve capacity.

Ben/Evelyn — please send the calendar invite for 10am PT tomorrow and include the Drive link and short pre-read. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Priya
SVP, Product
Horizon Dataworks
